judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked the letter promising no further payments after six instalments, which is precisely six months of payments; that letter appears to be the intended outcome of this review, and the two are only loosely joined.
judgments.clause_name: News Memorandum of Understanding, 1.C. Review of Schedule

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'More favorable terms or treatment with respect to the payment or disposition called for by an arbitration award or judicial decree' is a comparative standard applied to unrelated settlements, and 'the same terms shall be accorded' with automatic amendment is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked the Times damage judgment memorandum, in which The Times forgives its judgment entirely; that could be argued to be 'more favorable treatment' by another employer, though this clause speaks of other labor organizations.
judgments.clause_name: News Memorandum of Understanding, 1.D. More Favorable Terms

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite obligation to withdraw an identified suit on execution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with paragraph 1's payment arrangement and paragraph 3's acceleration remedy.
judgments.clause_name: News Memorandum of Understanding, 2. Withdrawal of Suit

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Violates the provisions against strikes and disruptions of orderly relationships' describes the triggering breach loosely — 'disruptions of orderly relationships' has no counterpart in the Agreement's text — and the final sentence is grammatically incomplete ('penalties for any future violations ... to seek and obtain').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 16-N, which prohibits strikes, lockouts 'or other cessation of work or interference therewith' but says nothing of 'orderly relationships'; the mismatch between the acceleration trigger and the operative no-strike clause is a genuine problem.
judgments.clause_name: News Memorandum of Understanding, 3. Acceleration on Violation

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any major change in its operations which has an impact on a significant number of its NMDU employees' stacks two vague qualifiers, with only a parenthetical example to guide them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 16-M.3, which requires prior consent for any change in condition, and 20-E.2's notice of Bulldog phase-out; a thirty-day notice obligation for major changes reads as an alternative to a consent requirement, which is a real tension.
judgments.clause_name: Memorandum — Thirty Days Notice of Major Change

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The memorandum directs an arbitrator to render a written decision 'in accordance with his earlier oral opinion' setting out three points from a 1971 decision in another arbitration — none of which are reproduced, so the content of the interpretation is entirely outside the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 16-M.3, whose 'no change in condition' phrase this memorandum exists to construe, and 16-M.5's exclusive change-of-conditions Board; the need for this memorandum is itself evidence that 16-M is contested, and the incorporated points are unknowable from the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Every memorandum, letter agreement or side agreement shall be continued through the term of this agreement and deemed updated' is a sweeping catch-all, and 'deemed updated' has no ascertainable meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 21-B.4 and 21-G.3, which state expiration dates, and 21-D.VIII's supersession clause; a blanket continuation of every side agreement contradicts both the express expirations and the Newspoint supersession provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A preamble identifying the parties, date and subject matter, with the statement that it 'is within the terms of the current collective bargaining agreement'; that last assertion is a conclusion rather than a rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 17-D's settlement recital and 22-A's Carlstadt provisions, which the Supplementary Agreement supplements; declaring the memorandum 'within the terms' of the main agreement can be tested against provisions like 16-M.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arithmetic in the parenthetical does not close: two new situations of five nights and of four days plus one night, 'and one additional shift (a total of 11 shifts)' — 5 + 5 = 10, so the extra shift and the total require explanation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 22-A's floor-operations minimum and 5-D's night work week of three short nights, one long night and Saturday; a five-night situation and a four-day-plus-one-night situation must be fitted to 5-C/5-D's structures, which is not addressed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'may assign, as needed the utility man to jobs, including but not limited to' is an express open-ended catch-all, and the missing comma and the exclusivity sentence ('clearing log jams ... may only be performed by the utility man (exclusive of foremen)') create a rule that could conflict with normal manning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 22-A's Control Room clause reserving console work to delivery department journeymen and 21-D.III's manning; an exclusive log-jam assignment to a single utility man is hard to reconcile with continuous operations when he is absent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph is dense and internally qualified: an eighty-one floor-hire minimum, excluding 'the "Alco Men" or people performing functions other than regular floor work', six chauffeur-available floormen 'provided all areas are properly manned', and a proportional reduction clause that presupposes a reduction the first sentence appears to forbid.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 22-A's minimum-one-floorman rule and 4-A.2's shape and priority hiring, expressly preserved in the last sentence; the eighty-one minimum coupled with a reduction mechanism and a priority-hiring saving clause is genuinely hard to harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The guarantee is definite in substance but the text is corrupted ('a chiage in starting times', 'the nar..ed individuals', 'wir a job'), and 'so long as the named individuals maintain their present jobs' leaves the class fixed by reference to an unattached list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 5-J, which allows starting-time changes on four days' notice, and 20-E.7, which gives Publishers discretion over starting times on Bulldog phase-out; an absolute guarantee against starting-time changes conflicts with both.
judgments.clause_name: Supplementary Agreement, 4. Guarantee of Starting Times

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'He will be paid an extra half hour at the required rate' leaves 'the required rate' unspecified (straight time or overtime), and the exclusion where 'the starting point and finishing point are the same' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 5-L, which requires travel-time compensation to be negotiated or arbitrated, and 13-D's overtime rate; this half hour partly implements 5-L but the rate ambiguity connects to 13-D.
judgments.clause_name: Supplementary Agreement, 5. Trailer Driver Drop at Carlstadt

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-off delivery obligation as of the signing date; definite though limited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked the letter on posting job descriptions including starting times and days off, and 5-J's list obligation; consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Supplementary Agreement, 6. Job Descriptions to Chairman

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Provides a named vehicle type for two named individuals' job; concrete but tied to specific persons with no provision for succession.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 3-K's obligation to furnish all delivery equipment; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific commitment to establish Saturday direct delivery to Albany 'as it does during the week'; clear, with no stated deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 2-E.2(e)(1), which requires Albany runs to be driven through by unit employees, and 3-F's freedom as to new routes; consistent.
judgments.clause_name: News Shop Conditions Memorandum, 1. Albany Direct Delivery

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Once a month, The News will have a doctor available evenings to give DOT examinations' is precise as to frequency though vague as to duration and location.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 14-C on discharge for a bad driving record and 3-H.1's vehicle safety obligations; the examination facility supports those and conflicts with nothing.
judgments.clause_name: News Shop Conditions Memorandum, 2. DOT Examinations

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dated obligation to establish a seven-day Manhattan route, with the printed 'Such route shall be filed by in-shop bidding' evidently a typo for 'filled'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 4-B's posting-and-bidding procedure and 21-C.3(f)'s new franchise jobs; in-shop bidding is consistent with Section 4's framework.
judgments.clause_name: News Shop Conditions Memorandum, 3. Manhattan Route

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'posting job descriptions including, but not limited to, starting times and days off and job functions' uses an express non-exhaustive formula, and the closing sentence that these practices 'do not limit either party's rights under the collective bargaining agreement' is a broad neutralising disclaimer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 5-J's list of starting times and days off and the Supplementary Agreement paragraph 6's job-description delivery; the disclaimer leaves it unclear whether posted descriptions bind, which interacts with 16-M.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parity promise is broad ('whatever increase, however formulated') and the exceptions are vague — improvements granted 'in exchange for productivity improvements (as determined to the Union's reasonable satisfaction)' or 'diverted from the negotiated pattern package', the latter phrase having no defined content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 21-F.3's comparable-improvements clause for News pensions and 3-M's most-favoured-terms provision; three overlapping parity mechanisms with different wording invite argument about which governs a given benefit increase.
judgments.clause_name: Letter — Pension, Welfare and Insurance Benefit Parity

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear holdover rule for the status quo and alternate status quo arbitrators until replacements are selected and have assumed office.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 16-G, which terminates the permanent impartial chairmen's term on expiration of the Agreement, and 16-M.1's annual selection dates; a holdover 'until the parties select a replacement' contradicts those fixed terms.
judgments.clause_name: Letter — Status Quo Arbitrator and Arbitrator List, 1

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A holdover rule for the arbitrator list until a new list is selected and the new arbitrators accept; definite in mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 16-E.2's requirement to select fifteen arbitrators 'immediately after the execution of this Agreement' with a sixty-day AAA fallback, and 16-E.3's striking rights; a continuation of the old list sits against those mandatory deadlines.
judgments.clause_name: Letter — Status Quo Arbitrator and Arbitrator List, 2

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An option exercisable on sixty days' written notice, with the choice of weekly or bi-weekly left to the Union; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 2-N.1, which provides for monthly deduction from the second pay check; this letter expressly amends that provision rather than contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely a notification that The Times 'is happy to continue our discussions'; it creates no measurable obligation at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 17-D's recital that the parties have bargained and settled all terms for the contract term; an open commitment to continue pension discussions sits against that settlement recital, though it stops short of an obligation to bargain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Times has agreed to discussion concerning the feasibility of this proposal before the operation begins' is a bare agreement to discuss, with the qualifier 'providing such transport did not involve the Times in increased costs' left as a condition on a proposal not yet agreed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 9-B's parallel 'endeavour ... providing doing so does not involve the Publisher in increased cost' formula and 17-D's settlement recital; the cost-escape language is a consistent pattern, but the agreement to discuss cuts against 17-D.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The commitment dissolves into conditions: 'will discuss with Citibank', 'If a sufficient number of employees are interested', and 'Citibank (or another acceptable bank) will be permitted' — no party is bound to establish anything despite the opening sentence saying a program will be established.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked the Credit Union Checkoff letter, which contains a firm deduction and remittance obligation; the contrast shows this letter's commitment is markedly softer, and the two savings mechanisms are unrelated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The equipment commitments are itemised and concrete, but 'All trucks used for over-the-road runs (Long Island routes, news company runs, all other long runs)' ends in an undefined catch-all, and 'all other long runs' has no boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 3-H.1's requirement that all motor vehicles be equipped with heaters and defrosters maintained in good working condition; this letter promises under-the-seat heaters only in new trucks and maintenance of existing ones, which is arguably narrower than 3-H.1's blanket obligation.
judgments.clause_name: Letter — Heaters, Bostrum Seats and Safety Equipment

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'When the six payments referred to in the Memorandum have been made ... The News will not, under any circumstances, require additional payments' is emphatic, but the Memorandum does not itself speak of 'six payments', so the trigger is identified by a reference that does not match.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked the News Memorandum paragraphs 1 and 1.A, which oblige payment of the full $177,844 principal in $1,250 monthly instalments, and 1.C's six-month review; forgiveness after six payments squarely contradicts the obligation to pay the whole sum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The printed text is scrambled and the operative sentences are separated by intervening page matter, but the commitments — abide by the 48-inch skid-height award and by 'all Newspoint written agreements' — are clear, the latter being an unbounded catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 21-D.VIII, which supersedes all other agreements, memoranda or practices applicable to the Newspoint operation; a promise to abide by all Newspoint written agreements directly contradicts that supersession clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A deleted memorandum is made applicable 'should there be a problem in the future arising thereunder' — a conditional revival of text not reproduced anywhere in the instrument, so its content is unknowable and the trigger is vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked the memorandum continuing every side agreement 'through the term of this agreement and deemed updated' and 17-D's settlement recital; reviving a deleted memorandum on an undefined contingency is difficult to reconcile with a contract said to contain the settled terms.
judgments.clause_name: Letter — Effect of Labor Dispute on Eligibility Requirements

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation is only to post notice of 'such rules of eligibility' for 'the Medill Plan' within thirty days; the plan name appears garbled and the rules themselves are not stated, so the substance is external.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 13-H's Welfare Fund provisions and the letter on labor-dispute eligibility requirements; the eligibility rules for benefit plans are treated as extrinsic throughout, so this fits the pattern.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deduction duty is clear but the amount and duration are left to the employee's designation and to an assignment 'satisfactory to the Publisher' — a unilateral approval standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 2-N.1's dues checkoff mechanics and 2-N.2's Section 302 qualifier; a credit-union deduction is a separate stream and I found no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Publishers acknowledge that the collective bargaining agreement prohibits the subcontracting of bargaining unit deliveries except as it may exist pursuant to the contract' is circular: the exception swallows the acknowledgment and no prohibition is located in any numbered provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 3-E's methods-and-extent freeze, 3-F's freedom for new routes and 9-B's endeavour-subject-to-cost formula; whether the contract in fact contains a subcontracting prohibition is precisely what those provisions leave open, so this acknowledgment asserts more than the text supplies.
judgments.clause_name: Letter — Clarification of Method and Extent

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two commitments, one preserving an unstated 'present practice' of separate vacation checks and one requiring an annual statement of shifts credited to the Joint Pension Fund; the practice reference has no content on the page.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 22-B on Times vacation-check withholding and 13-I.1's contribution base; the shift statement supports verification of 13-I.1 and I found no conflict.
judgments.clause_name: Letter — Vacation Checks and Pension Shift Statement

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three of the four obligations are conditioned on installation of an unspecified 'planned DEC System', with no date, so the timing of performance is wholly indeterminate; the interim posting obligation is concrete by contrast.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 13-I.1's pension contributions and the parallel Times letter, which imposes an unconditional annual statement duty; conditioning The News' duty on an undated system installation creates an asymmetry but not a contradiction.
judgments.clause_name: Letter — DEC System, Separate Vacation Checks and Pension Statements

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A thirty-day deadline subject to an exception 'if delayed because of an emergency or Act of God' — a general excuse paired with an undefined 'emergency', which is exactly the kind of escape clause that gets tested.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 13-A.1's effective date of March 31, 1981 and 13-A.5's wage-controls termination right; retroactive payment on ratification is consistent with the wage schedule's effective date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A preamble reciting that sub-committee members 'discussed and agreed upon the following', which leaves unclear whether the items are binding agreements or minutes of discussion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked the items that follow (A.1-3, B, C.1-4), several of which are plainly non-binding ('would explore', 'agreed to meet and discuss'), and the memorandum continuing all side agreements; the binding status of these 1978 minutes in a 1981-84 book is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — New York News Sub-Committee, Preamble

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Union requested ... and was advised that such vans would be ordered' is reportage of a representation, not a promise, and creates no clear obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked item B, which reports vans with side doors 'already ordered', and 3-K's equipment-furnishing duty; the minute is descriptive and consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — News, A. Brooklyn, 1. Vans

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'would explore the purchase and use of dehumidifiers' is an agreement to explore with no standard or outcome.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 3-H.1's undue-hardship and adverse-weather protections; an obligation only to explore is weaker than 3-H.1's 'measures shall be taken, insofar as practicable', which is a mild tension.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — News, A. Brooklyn, 2. Dehumidifiers

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the same as the men in the New York plant for handling three-part inserts (500 or more)' is specific as to the comparator and the threshold, though 'the same' leaves the underlying rate to external practice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 13-A's uniform rate schedules for all signatory Publishers; an inter-plant parity promise for a particular task is consistent with those schedules.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — News, A. Brooklyn, 3. Three-Part Inserts

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Company indicated that new trucks had been ordered' is purely a report of a statement, with no obligation created at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 3-K's equipment obligation and item A.1; the minute is informational and consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — News, B. New York

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'sixers' is unexplained trade shorthand and 'in the same percentage as they are currently available to the Newspoint day shift' fixes the entitlement by an unstated current ratio.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 21-D.III's day-side manning and 21-D.VI's day-side employment guarantee; the percentage parity depends on facts those provisions do not supply.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — News, C. Newspoint, 1. Sixers

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Five jobs are named for definition on posting, but the clause records only that they 'would be defined when posted' — the definitions themselves are absent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 4-B's posting requirements and the letter on posting job descriptions including starting times, days off and job functions; those supply the posting framework consistently.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — News, C. Newspoint, 2. Five Jobs Defined

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Union agreed to meet and discuss the printing of commercial sheets' is an agreement to meet with no substantive content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 21-D.V, which allocates handling of commercial work at Newspoint and disapplies 3-L's extra-crew rule; an agreement to discuss printing sits alongside that allocation without conflict.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — News, C. Newspoint, 3. Commercial Sheets

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to meet within thirty days 'to discuss shop level problems' — indeterminate in subject and outcome.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 16-A, which requires plant-level settlement attempts before referral; a shop-level meeting commitment fits that scheme.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — News, C. Newspoint, 4. Shop Level Meeting

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same recital form ('discussed and agreed upon the following'), with the printed text badly interleaved with marginal noise, leaving the binding character of the minutes unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked the three items that follow, which are relatively concrete, and the memorandum continuing side agreements; whether November 1978 sub-committee minutes remain operative in the 1981-84 term is unresolved.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — New York Times Sub-Committee, Preamble

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Two new console jobs will be created at the Carlstadt facility (one day job; one night job)' is concrete as to number and shift.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 22-A's Control Room clause reserving console work to delivery department journeymen and the Supplementary Agreement's utility-man console relief; consistent, though the relationship between these console jobs and the later utility man is not addressed.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — Times, 1. Console Jobs

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific new run with a six-day schedule, an 11:00 p.m. start and inter-shop bidding; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked 5-D's night work week of five nights (three short, one long, Saturday) against a 'six-day run', and 4-B's bidding; a six-day run must be squared with the five-shift week and 2-L.3's sixth-shift premium.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — Times, 2. Atlantic City Run

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reviewed within a reasonable time ... but in no event later than sixty (60) days' cures the vagueness with an outer limit, but 'reviewed' states no outcome or standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked the Supplementary Agreement paragraph 3's combined floor-hire minimum for both plants and 22-A's floor-operations minimum; a bare review commitment leaves manning at 43rd Street to those provisions.
judgments.clause_name: Letter of Understanding — Times, 3. Manning at 43rd Street
